scientific_limitations: Testing bodies must be full-dimensional convex polytopes and the probability law must have compact support.
The general facet-width/slack threshold is sufficient, not necessarily optimal.
Parallelotope cutoff is sharp as a distribution-uniform guarantee, not for every individual law.
Strict projected halfspaces are required in the presence of atoms.
Full historical priority and independent mathematical validation are not established.
title: Finite-scale stabilization of polyhedral translate depth and its sharp box cutoff
